name: August Wi-Fi Smart Lock Gen 4 (US)

radios.note: Built-in Wi-Fi for remote and voice control; Bluetooth for local operation and for talking to HomeKit.

matter.note: No official Matter statement found. A Best Buy Canada spec sheet lists Matter as unsupported, but retailer data is not enough to mark it 'no'.

apple_home.note: HomeKit over Bluetooth. Controlling it away from home needs an Apple home hub (Apple TV, HomePod or iPad). No Home Key mentioned.

google_home.note: Google Assistant integration needs the lock on Wi-Fi.

alexa.note: Needs Wi-Fi. Voice unlock requires setting a PIN.

smartthings.note: August's Wi-Fi Smart Lock FAQ and its older integrations pages list Samsung SmartThings (cloud integration, no Z-Wave), but the current product page does not, and no SmartThings page confirms the integration is still offered.

home_assistant.note: The August integration lists the Wi-Fi Smart Lock (Gen 4) as working with no Connect Bridge. Gen 4 battery readings are often wrong in Home Assistant.

hubRequired.note: Wi-Fi is built in; August says no bridge is needed. Remote HomeKit use still needs an Apple home hub.

localControl.note: Bluetooth control from the app is local, but no source confirms local control through any smart home platform.

lockFit.note: Mounts over the interior side of your existing deadbolt, so your outside hardware and keys stay.

keypad.note: No keypad on the lock; Yale/August sell keypad versions as separate products.

power.note: August's FAQ says two 3V CR123 or CR123A lithium (non-rechargeable) cells, with up to 3 months of life under typical Wi-Fi use. The 4 × AA seen on some listings belongs to older August locks.

summary: The August Wi-Fi Smart Lock (4th gen) fits over the inside of your existing deadbolt, so your outside hardware and keys stay, and it has Wi-Fi built in with no bridge. Apple Home works over Bluetooth, Google Home and Alexa need the lock on Wi-Fi, and Home Assistant's August integration lists it. No Matter support is confirmed and SmartThings status is unclear. Two CR123A cells last about 3 months with typical Wi-Fi use.
caveats: Battery life is short: August cites up to 3 months of typical Wi-Fi use on two CR123A cells.
Away-from-home control through Apple Home needs an Apple TV, HomePod or iPad as a home hub.
Alexa voice unlock requires setting a PIN.
Gen 4 battery readings are often wrong in Home Assistant.
There is no keypad on the lock; keypads are sold separately.
